title: 1977 AHSME Problem 11
statement:
For each real number \(x,\) let \([x]\) be the largest integer not exceeding \(x\) (i.e., the integer \(n\) such that \(n\le x\lt n+1\)). Which of the following statements is (are) true?

\(\mathrm{I}.\) \([x+1]=[x]+1\) for all \(x\)

\(\mathrm{II}.\) \([x+y]=[x]+[y]\) for all \(x\) and \(y\)

\(\mathrm{III}.\) \([xy]=[x][y]\) for all \(x\) and \(y\)

solutions.text:
If \(n\le x\lt n+1,\) then \(n+1\le x+1\lt n+2,\) so \(\mathrm{I}\) is true. Taking \(x=y=\frac{3}{2}\) gives \([x+y]=3\ne2=[x]+[y]\) and \([xy]=2\ne1=[x][y].\) Thus \(\mathrm{II}\) and \(\mathrm{III}\) are false.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Prove the translation statement directly from \(n\le x\lt n+1\)
Test the other two claims using noninteger values between \(1\) and \(2\)
